subject: english-literature
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the assessment objectives.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Why did Mr Birling first cause harm to Eva Smith?
options: He sacked her for asking for higher wages
He reported her to the Inspector
questions.explain: Birling dismissed Eva from his factory for leading a request for a pay rise.

questions.q: What relationship did Gerald Croft have with Daisy Renton?
options: He kept her as his mistress for a time
questions.explain: Gerald had an affair with Daisy Renton, keeping her for several months before ending it.

questions.q: Which characters are most changed by the Inspector's visit?
options: Sheila and Eric, the younger generation
questions.explain: The younger Birlings accept their guilt, while their parents largely refuse to change.

questions.q: Mr Birling's confident speeches about the Titanic being "unsinkable" are an example of what dramatic technique?
questions.explain: The audience knows the Titanic sank, making Birling's claims ironic and undermining his judgement.

questions.q: What does Inspector Goole warn will happen if people do not learn the lesson of responsibility?
options: They will be taught it "in fire and blood and anguish"
questions.explain: His final speech warns that ignoring social responsibility leads to suffering "in fire and blood and anguish".

questions.q: What central message does Inspector Goole deliver about society?
options: That "we are members of one body" and responsible for one another
That the rich deserve their wealth
That the law solves all problems
questions.explain: The Inspector argues people are responsible for each other, the play's theme of social responsibility.

questions.q: How was Eric Birling involved with Eva Smith?
options: He fathered her unborn child and stole money to support her
He reported her to his father
questions.explain: Eric had a relationship with Eva, got her pregnant, and took money from the firm to help her.

questions.q: In An Inspector Calls, what is the occasion at the Birling household when the play opens?
questions.explain: The family is celebrating the engagement of Sheila Birling to Gerald Croft.

questions.q: What is the name of the young woman whose death the Inspector investigates?
questions.explain: The dead girl is Eva Smith, who also went by the name Daisy Renton.

questions.q: How was Sheila Birling responsible for Eva Smith's misfortune?
options: She reported her to the police
She had Eva dismissed from a shop out of jealousy
questions.explain: Sheila got Eva sacked from Milwards in a fit of jealous temper.

questions.q: How did Mrs Birling contribute to Eva Smith's death?
options: She used her influence to deny Eva help from a charity
She sacked her from a shop
She gave her too much money
questions.explain: As head of a charity, Mrs Birling refused the pregnant Eva assistance and blamed the father.

questions.q: Mr Birling can be seen to represent which political viewpoint?
questions.explain: Birling champions individual profit and dismisses community, embodying capitalist values Priestley critiques.
